title: Balanced Team (Codeforces 1133C)
statement:
A coach has `n` students, and student `i` has a skill rating `a[i]`. The coach wants to pick a team that is as large as possible. A team is **balanced** if the ratings of any two members differ by **at most 5**.

Print the maximum possible size of a balanced team. A team of a single student is always balanced, and students with equal ratings may all be chosen.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
output_format: Print one integer: the maximum size of a balanced team.

examples.explanation: The ratings 4, 5, 8 and 9 have a largest difference of 9 - 4 = 5, so they form a balanced team of 4. No team of 5 exists.
Every pair differs by more than 5, so the best team has a single student.
All ratings are equal, so everyone can join.

hints: A team is balanced exactly when its largest rating minus its smallest rating is at most 5. The order of the students does not matter, so sort the ratings.
After sorting, an optimal team can be taken as a contiguous block of the sorted array.
Slide a window with two pointers: extend the right end, and move the left end while `a[right] - a[left] > 5`. Track the largest window.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = sorted(int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n])
    best = 0
    left = 0
    for right in range(n):
        while a[right] - a[left] > 5:
            left += 1
        if right - left + 1 > best:
            best = right - left + 1
    print(best)

main()
